description:
Found during the bedrock-61c.3 audit; pre-existing and currently unreachable.

lib/bedrock/data_plane/log/shale/segment_recycler.ex — `Server.handle_call({:check_out, ...})`:

    {:ok, state}          -> reply(state, :ok, continue: :ensure_min_available)
    {:error, _reason} = e -> reply(state, e)

The success path schedules the min-refill; the failure path does not. `Logic.check_out/2` returns `{:error, :unavailable}` exactly when `segments: []`, so the one moment the pool most needs refilling is the one moment it is not scheduled. Nothing else drives `:ensure_min_available` except a successful checkout, so an emptied pool never recovers on its own — every subsequent checkout fails, and `Segment.allocate_from_recycler!/4` raises.

Currently unreachable: `check_out` is always followed by a refill that restores `min_available` before the next message, and check-in never shrinks the pool. It becomes reachable if allocation ever fails transiently (a full disk that later clears) — the pool would be stuck at zero with no path back even after space returns.

## Fix

Schedule `:ensure_min_available` on the error path too.

## Test (write first, must fail)

Construct a recycler state with an empty pool, call `handle_call({:check_out, path}, ...)`, and assert the reply carries `{:continue, :ensure_min_available}` alongside the error.
title: [BUG] SegmentRecycler never refills after a failed check_out, so an emptied pool stays empty
